nodes.title: What makes parts equal
nodes.objective: The learner can draw a shape split into equal parts and explain why the parts must be the same size.
nodes.misconception: Draws any division of the shape and calls each section a fraction regardless of whether the parts are equal in size.
nodes.check: Show four shapes — two split correctly, two not. Ask the class to sort them and explain one wrong one.

nodes.title: Fractions on the number line
nodes.objective: The learner can place 1/2, 1/4 and 3/4 on a number line between 0 and 1.
nodes.misconception: Places fractions out of order because the bottom number is treated as if bigger means further along.
nodes.check: Hand out a blank 0-to-1 strip. Ask the class to place three fractions. One wrong placement means the misconception is still active.

nodes.title: Bigger bottom number, smaller piece
nodes.objective: The learner can say whether 1/3 or 1/5 is bigger and explain why.
nodes.misconception: Says 1/5 is bigger because 5 is bigger than 3.
nodes.check: Which is a bigger share of a pizza — 1/3 or 1/6? Correct answer with a plain explanation: the idea has landed.

nodes.title: Equivalent fractions: same value, different look
nodes.objective: The learner can write two fractions that are equivalent and show why using a diagram.
nodes.misconception: Adds the same number to both top and bottom instead of multiplying.
nodes.check: Show me 2/4 and 1/2 on a strip — are they the same? A correct diagram with explanation: the idea has landed.

nodes.title: Simplifying fractions
nodes.objective: The learner can write 4/8 in its simplest form.
nodes.misconception: Divides only the top number, or only the bottom number.
nodes.check: What is the simplest way to write 6/9? Ask the class to show the step.

nodes.title: Unit 1 consolidation
nodes.objective: The learner can identify the two main errors from the unit and correct them.
nodes.misconception: Applies both errors in the same question without noticing.
nodes.check: One question requiring both skills. Mini-whiteboard show — scan for both specific errors.

nodes.title: Why you cannot add the bottoms
nodes.objective: The learner can explain why 1/2 + 1/3 does not equal 2/5.
nodes.misconception: Adds the tops together and the bottoms together.
nodes.check: Someone said 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5. What did they do wrong? Correct identification: the idea has landed.

nodes.title: Finding a common denominator
nodes.objective: The learner can find the lowest common denominator for two fractions.
nodes.misconception: Multiplies the two denominators together every time, missing the lowest requirement.
nodes.check: What is the lowest common denominator of 1/4 and 1/6? Finding 12 by listing multiples: landed. Finding 24: revisit.

nodes.title: Adding fractions with unlike denominators
nodes.objective: The learner can add two fractions with unlike denominators.
nodes.misconception: Converts one fraction correctly but forgets to convert the other before adding.
nodes.check: Three addition problems shown step by step. At least two correct with both conversions shown: landed.

nodes.title: Subtracting fractions with unlike denominators
nodes.objective: The learner can subtract two fractions with unlike denominators.
nodes.misconception: Subtracts the smaller denominator from the larger before converting.
nodes.check: Work out 3/4 − 1/3, showing every step. Both conversions shown and the subtraction correct: landed.

nodes.title: Mixed numbers: adding
nodes.objective: The learner can add two mixed numbers.
nodes.misconception: Adds whole numbers and fractions separately but forgets to recombine.
nodes.check: What is 1 and 1/2 + 2 and 1/3? Correct answer with clear working: landed.

nodes.title: Mixed numbers: subtracting (borrowing)
nodes.objective: The learner can subtract a fraction from a mixed number that requires borrowing.
nodes.misconception: Subtracts the fraction from the whole number directly without borrowing.
nodes.check: Work out 3 and 1/4 − 3/4, showing every step. Correct answer with borrowing shown: landed.

nodes.title: Word problems: fractions in context
nodes.objective: The learner can solve a one-step word problem involving fraction addition or subtraction.
nodes.misconception: Applies the wrong operation, or applies the right operation to the wrong pair of fractions.
nodes.check: Ask the learner to name what needs to be calculated before writing anything. Correct identification: landed.

nodes.title: Two-step fraction problems
nodes.objective: The learner can solve a two-step word problem involving fractions.
nodes.misconception: Stops after the first calculation, or conflates the two steps.
nodes.check: There are two things to work out here — what are they? If the learner can name both steps before starting: landed.

nodes.title: Unit 2 consolidation
nodes.objective: The learner can add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators without scaffolding.
nodes.misconception: Reverts to adding the bottoms under time pressure.
nodes.check: Four questions, no worked example. Two or more fully correct with working: unit objective has landed.

nodes.title: Review and catch-up
nodes.objective: The learner can identify and correct their own main error from the unit.
nodes.misconception: Varies by learner — the check identifies which type.
nodes.check: Return one marked piece of work. Ask the learner to name their error and correct one question.

nodes.title: Connecting equivalent fractions to addition
nodes.objective: The learner can explain the connection between finding a common denominator and finding equivalent fractions.
nodes.misconception: Treats them as two separate procedures with no relation.
nodes.check: When you found the common denominator for 1/2 + 1/3, what did you do to 1/2? If the learner can say 'made it equivalent': landed.

nodes.title: End-of-unit assessment
nodes.objective: The learner can demonstrate the three unit outcomes.
nodes.misconception: Reverts to any of the three main errors: adding bottoms, single-fraction conversion, or borrowing.
nodes.check: One question per outcome, completed independently. Record by outcome.
